newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firmer for 4th straight session.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firmer for 4th straight session.

text.p: Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed firmer for the fourth session in a row on Wednesday and broke resistance at 7.80 per dollar as foreign capital flowed into Mexico, traders said.
"Someone out there wanted to put the peso under pressure, but dollars were in supply," one trader said.

"Trading rates did see-saw, but within a narrow range," another trader said. The 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.55 and 0.6 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.7880/7.7940 and 7.7850/7.7900 per dollar.
Dealers said minor changes in primary interest rates at Tuesday night's weekly central bank auction helped bolster the peso.
Rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) fell just five basis points from last week to 22.93 percent.
The market will now be looking out for inflation figures for the first half of January, which the central bank was expected to announce on Thursday.

A Reuters survey of 11 Mexico City financial firms MXAAP showed an average forecast of 1.24 percent inflation for Jan 1-15. Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.8 of a centavo firmer at 7.7850/7.7900 per dollar.
